name: Office of Future Plans
label: Dischord
lede: J. Robbins said yes to one opening slot in Baltimore, put a cello where the second guitar usually goes, and woke up seven years later with a band and a Dischord album he'd recorded in his own studio.

eras.title: A favor that kept going
eras.text: By fall 2009 J. Robbins had fronted Jawbox, Burning Airlines and Channels and was running his own recording studio, the Magpie Cage, in Baltimore. The Bomb needed an opener, he built a band for the night, and nobody wanted to stop.

years.h: Callum Robbins is diagnosed with spinal muscular atrophy
years.p: J. Robbins' son Callum is diagnosed with SMA, an incurable nerve disorder, in 2007. Benefit shows follow for the Robbins family in Chicago, Washington, Minneapolis and New York.

years.cap: Office of Future Plans at Fort Reno, Washington, July 25, 2011
q: Office of Future Plans was never supposed to be a band.
years.src: Dischord: Office of Future Plans · Wikipedia: Office of Future Plans
years.h: A Baltimore opening slot for The Bomb becomes a band
years.p: Chicago punk band The Bomb asks J. Robbins to open a show in Baltimore. He recruits cellist and guitarist [[Gordon Withers|5af1786c-c098-428c-9aec-261e3c9c5705]], bassist [[Brooks Harlan|f9cb849f-568b-4987-b9cc-96e0e5d7d790]] and drummer [[Darren Zentek|68c31f7f-f2e8-4353-92b7-c7ebf47f404d]], ex-[[Kerosene 454|3689eda0-1b6d-43f3-83ad-e58211ae7a3a]], and the four keep going.
years.xp:
Dischord dates the show to fall 2009 and says it was meant to be a one-off. Instead the four kept writing and arranging at the Magpie Cage, and the label says the songs got more collaborative and more layered as they went.

The line-up put a cello where a Jawbox fan would expect a second guitar, with Withers switching between cello and guitar.

eras.title: The Magpie Cage album
eras.text: The four wrote and arranged in Robbins' own studio. A crowdfunded single came first, then twelve songs on Dischord, the label that had put out Jawbox's records two decades earlier.

years.cap: J. Robbins at the Black Cat, Washington, Feb 20, 2010
years.src: Dischord: Office of Future Plans · Dischord: 2-song 7"
yt: Harden Your Heart and more, D.C., 2011
years.h: A Kickstarter-funded 7" in an edition of 500
years.p: The two-song single pairs "Harden Your Heart" with a Stranglers cover. Germany's Arctic Rodeo Recordings later repress it on colored vinyl.
years.xp: Dischord's band history says the DIY single was funded through Kickstarter. The band put it out themselves, 500 copies, before the album.

years.src: Dischord: Office of Future Plans (Dischord 173) · Wikipedia: Office of Future Plans
years.h: Twelve songs from the Magpie Cage land as Dischord No. 173
years.p: Dan Coutant masters the band's only album, which runs from "Salamander" to "Riddle Me This" with "Fema Coffins" somewhere in the middle.
years.xp: Dischord lists November 21, 2011; Wikipedia gives November 12. The songs were recorded at Robbins' own Magpie Cage, the same room where the band had rehearsed for two years.

years.h: "Lorelei" at the Rock and Roll Hotel, May 28, 2011
yt: "Lorelei" at the Rock and Roll Hotel, May 28, 2011

eras.title: A split, then no announcement
eras.text: One more record, a split with Daria, and then silence. There was no farewell show; the end surfaced in a Creative Loafing interview.

years.cap: Office of Future Plans at the Black Cat, Washington, March 8, 2013
years.h: A split with Daria comes out on Lovitt
years.p: Office of Future Plans share a record with Daria on Lovitt Records, the D.C.-area label that had long worked with Dischord bands.

years.cap: J. Robbins at the Black Cat, Washington, March 8, 2013
years.h: Robbins tells Creative Loafing the band is done
years.p: The news comes out in an October 2016 interview. Dischord lists the band's years as 2009 to 2016.

eras.title: Robbins goes solo, then back to Jawbox
eras.text: After Office of Future Plans, Robbins made a solo record and then reunited Jawbox. Brooks Harlan ended up there too.

years.p: The record comes out in 2019, three years after Office of Future Plans ended.

years.h: Jawbox hit the road for the first time in over twenty years
years.p: The band J. Robbins fronted before Office of Future Plans plays its first tour in more than twenty years.

years.h: Brooks Harlan takes the second guitar in Jawbox
years.p: When [[Bill Barbot|c0407a04-3b21-4274-9ed1-695fbc07b218]] leaves, Harlan, Robbins' bandmate in Office of Future Plans and a guitarist in [[War on Women|69c05e9a-883b-4570-9c3d-c4bfc896a488]], steps in.
years.xp: Barbot left citing the long commute from his new home in Vermont. Harlan, a longtime Robbins collaborator, took the second-guitar spot, so a piece of Office of Future Plans now plays in Jawbox.
